title: Quantization adaptor lifecycle and regression sentinel
creator: Leah Park
description: Define and implement a robust lifecycle for quantization artifacts (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) from intake through publishing and pinning, with a telemetry-first regression sentinel that automatically rejects or throttles risky variants. This ticket covers a new compatibility-hash approach for deterministic provenance, a microbenchmark + real-workload validation wave, and a canary gating policy that ties to SLO and quality deltas. The goal is to reduce silent perf regressions and make pin promotion safe and automated for typical hosted and dedicated flows.
acceptance_criteria: Quant artifact metadata includes deterministic compatibility_hash and source_provenance fields
Onboarding pipeline runs synthetic microbench and at least one real workload eval before artifact is eligible for canary
Regression sentinel computes latency and quality deltas vs pinned revision and emits PASS/WARN/FAIL decisions according to contract
Canary policy supports shadow-run, 1% traffic, and automated rollback when FAIL observed
Published artifacts are annotated in catalog with recommended pin (or 'do-not-pin') and reasoning
implementation_notes: Key pieces: (1) Intake adaptor to normalize artifacts from upstream (GPTQ/AWQ exporters, internal FP8 packer) and compute compatibility_hash by hashing model config + quant params + kernel ABI; (2) Validation harness: quick microbench (token/s, memory), deterministic unit tests, plus a sampled real-workload eval using existing eval-suite; (3) Sentinel: streaming comparator that aggregates p50/p95 latency, throughput, token-cost, and discrete semantic quality scores (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-specific evals) over the canary window and produces deterministic verdicts; (4) Publishing flow: artifact metadata writer + catalog indexer + pin-suggester service; (5) Rollout controller: integrates with routing to perform shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% promotion with autoskip on FAIL. Implementation should reuse existing telemetry schema and the canary metrics library. Document the compatibility_hash format and retention policy for probes and logs.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff — scoped microbench and compatibility_hash format. Drafted initial schema for artifact metadata.
2025-02-19: Prototype adapter that ingests GPTQ and AWQ tarballs and emits normalized manifest. Synthetic microbench implemented (single-GPU token/s measurement).

2025-02-20: Telemetry team reviewed metric set. Decided on p95 latency, relative token-cost, and a percent-fidelity metric as primary signals. Added a small real-workload sample harness using the 'conversational-core' prompt set.
2025-02-21: First end-to-end run for an INT8 variant completed. Sentinel flagged a 12% p95 regression vs pinned — manual inspection showed kernel fallback on a specific attention pattern.
2025-02-22: Determined mitigation: add kernel ABI marker to manifest so runtime picks optimized path. Created follow-up ENG-49602 to land kernel ABI marker in runtime.
comments: PM feedback (R. Gomez): Ensure the sentinel verdict includes a human-readable rationale field for SRE/PM review before auto-promotion.
Design feedback (M. Chen): Compatibility_hash must exclude ephemeral metadata (timestamps, CI run IDs). Suggest canonicalize config then SHA256.
Infra note (S. Patel): Microbench should run on the same machine class used in Dedicated pools to avoid false positives from differing GPU card performance.
Review (J. Rivera): Add a 'do-not-pin' lint that prevents pin-suggester from recommending variants that degrade semantic fidelity by >2% on the canonical eval set.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish artifact to staging catalog (do-not-pin by default) 2) Run shadow traffic for 24h, collect sentinel signals 3) If PASS, open canary: 1% traffic for 3 hours -> measure -> 10% for 6 hours -> measure -> promote. If WARN, require manual review and extended shadow. If FAIL, mark artifact 'quarantine' and auto-create rollback ticket.
fallback_policy: When sentinel returns FAIL during any step, route to pinned variant with exponential backoff; create an automated postmortem draft linked to artifact compatibility_hash. For WARN, throttle promotion and notify owners.
telemetry_contract: metric:latency.p95 — compare relative change vs baseline (threshold: +10% FAIL, +5% WARN)
log:kernel.fallback.count — any non-zero during canary -> WARN
event:compatibility_hash_mismatch — immediate FAIL for pinned traffic
risks: False positives from microbench mismatch with production workload leading to overly conservative rejections
Fingerprint collisions if compatibility_hash composition is incorrect
Latency spikes due to kernel ABI mismatch not detectable in short windows
Increased onboarding time if real-workload evals are too slow — need to balance cost vs safety
next_steps: Finish compatibility_hash spec and publish manifest template (owner: Aaron Mitchell)
Land API for artifact metadata writer and indexer (PR #102 review)
Integrate sentinel with canary controller and test shadow-run flow for AWQ sample model
Follow-up: ENG-49602 to expose kernel ABI marker in runtime and update microbench harness to detect fallback counts
